what: Turns the California AB-32 cap-and-trade programme on or off. When on, a carbon allowance price is added to Pacific census division (division 9) delivered fuel prices for residential, commercial and transportation (from 2015) and to California industrial prices; California efficiency rebates are doubled in the commercial technology cost logic for division 9; the refinery model gets a California AB32 constraint and allowance cost; the electricity dispatch code maps California commercial efficiency savings and costs into the electricity region; EPM keeps its California cap inputs. In cb2026 the value is 1, so it is on.

values.meaning: AB-32 on: allowance price in division 9 fuel prices (util_copyadjusted.f90:696) and industrial prices (ind.f), commercial division 9 rebates doubled (comm.f:1911, 1937), AB32 constraint and allowance cost in the refinery model (lfmodel.gms:1171), California EE savings and costs mapped in the electricity code (uefd.f:1392, 1535), EPM keeps cap inputs from its data file (epm_read.py:618)
AB-32 off: none of the above; EPM sets the cap to 272.727, and offset, cost containment, reserve and auction prices to 0 (epm_read.py:618-624)

allowed: 0 or 1 (code tests ==1 in most places and >0 in uefd.f; description says 0=Off, 1=On)
notes: RTOVALUE default differs by file: 0 in comm.f and uaimms.f, 1 in ind.f, uefd.f, tran.f, refine*.f and util_copyadjusted.f90; EPM defaults to '1'. Moot while the key is present in MOREOPT (cb2026 sets 1). Refinery gets it through a GDX element (refine.f:1816 writes it, lfprep.gms:3713 loads it, lfmodel.gms makes the AB32 constraint and allowance cost conditional on it). util_copyadjusted adds the allowance cost to division 9 prices from 2015 and only when ab_allow_p is above 0. The commercial doubling and price adders use census division 9 (Pacific), not only California. In uefd.f the California efficiency mapping applies only when CO2_STDSW is 0 or before CO2_STDY1 (uefd.f:1535). The AIMMS EFD model declares AB32SW (efd.ams:298) and uaimms.f writes ed::AB32SW, but no AIMMS code uses the parameter, so the EFD optimiser itself does not read it. tran.f:1247 sets TRANAB32 but nothing else uses it, so Transportation is affected only through the delivered prices. resd.f has only a comment about it; Residential is affected only through prices.
correction: models/efd/MainProject/efd.ams:298 is the only AB32SW hit in models/efd and models/ecp (declaration only), so 'CA cap in electricity' was overstated; the 'Oil and gas supply' tag has no AB32SW reader and tran.f:1247 TRANAB32 is unused.

what: Sets the weight on the stored previous wellhead price when smoothing the perfect-foresight expected natural gas price against the price in the restart file, for each year from the first model year to LASTYR. Higher means the stored previous price counts for more and expectations move more slowly.

values.meaning: new value is a 50/50 average of the restart price and the stored previous price

allowed: percent 0 to 100 (code divides by 100)
notes: Only used when WELLPF = 1 (cb2026 sets 1). Formula (util_tools.f90:1014): new = restart price x (1 - w) + stored previous price x w, where the stored price is XOGWPRNGPF(2,...). If that stored price is zero or negative, line 1010 sets it to the restart price and the weight then changes nothing. values.meaning: WTI_PRICE after the last historical year is 0.98 * weight * last historical WTI + (1 - weight) * model crude price RFCRUDEWHP(2,1); the history weight starts at about 10 percent (times 0.98) and falls linearly to 0 by 2050 (refine.f:296-306)

WTI_PRICE is set directly to the model crude price RFCRUDEWHP(2,1) in every year the refinery model runs (2010 on); the guard 'curiyr+1989 .gt. HISTLYR' compares a calendar year with an index so it never blocks (refine_logs.f:286)

No history weight (WTIDECLINE is 0). WTI_PRICE equals the model crude price until HISTLYR+1989+12, then (1 + 2049/(2500*(2050-(HISTLYR+1990)))) times the model price through 2050, a constant markup of roughly 3 to 4 percent for a last historical year near 2025 (refine_hogs.f:296-306)

what: Scales how fast hydrogen electrolyzer capital costs fall relative to the Reference case (zero carbon technology cost cases). 1 keeps Reference behavior with normal endogenous learning. 0 freezes electrolyzer capital costs at their 2026 level (ZTCBasisYear) from 2026 on. A fraction between 0 and 1, or a whole number above 1 (read as a percent), gives a straight-line cut below the Reference capital costs, reaching that fraction in the last model year, starting from 2026.

values.meaning: Reference: capital costs and learning run as normal; the final model year's capital costs are written to CapitalCostsByYearReference.txt for the low case to read
electrolyzer capital costs held at the 2026 value (ZTCBasisYear) for all later years (code comment calls it the High ZTC case)

allowed: 0, a fraction between 0 and 1, 1, or a whole-number percent above 1 (divided by 100)
notes: Through this key the only consumer is the hydrogen model (HMM), via h2_runval.txt. Only electrolyzer technologies (prodTech_elec) are changed. The description says '1 = no exogenous learning', but the code says 1 means learning runs as normal; trust the code. Sending 100 gives 1.0 after division and behaves like Reference. The high/low labels follow the side-case names: highztc sets 0, lowztc sets 40. nems_hmm.ams:333 hard-codes ZTCCOSTM := 1.0 only in a standalone-AIMMS branch.
